# Results — Study 779 (Devil-Price)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **a
stock sitting on a "666" price level then underperforms** — rendered as a weekly
cross-sectional quintile sort of the S&P 100 on log-price distance to the nearest 666
handle. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce
every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month). Fingerprint
`b72f770274d9` (S&P 100 + SPY, one combined panel, adjusted/total-return daily closes).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, **S&P 100** universe + `SPY`, one combined panel: 4,903 rows, 2007-01-03 → 2026-06-30 |
| Universe | **hardcoded** S&P 100 (CBOE OEX) snapshot, 99 names; **98 returned data** (BK missing from Yahoo), + SPY as market benchmark |
| Characteristic | `devil_distance` = circular distance of `frac(log10 price)` to `log10 6.66` = 0.8235, in [0, 0.5] — decade-invariant, so $6.66 / $66.6 / $666 are all "on the beast" |
| Sort | weekly rebalance; quintiles by devil distance; **devil** leg = nearest quintile, **clean** leg = farthest; LS = clean − devil, cross-sectionally demeaned (market-neutral) |
| Rebalances | **976** weekly cross-sections, 2007-01-10 → 2026-05-28; cross-section size min/median/max = **88 / 98 / 98** |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the per-rebalance spread; Wilson hit-rate interval; a 20-seed × 100-draw random-**bucket** placebo per cut; leave-one-year-out jackknife; a non-overlapping monthly re-run |
| Horizons | forward simple return over 5 sessions (~1 week, **non-overlapping**) and 21 sessions (~1 month, weekly rebalance ⇒ ~4× overlap — flagged) |

**Overlap, named.** The 1-week sort rebalances every 5 sessions with a 5-day forward
window, so its rebalances barely overlap — its *t* is honest. The 1-month cut keeps the
weekly rebalance but a 21-day forward window, so consecutive windows overlap ~4×; its
naive *t* is inflated ~2× and must be read against the **non-overlapping monthly re-run**
below, which is the decisive test.

## The devil quintile — demeaned forward return (near-666 minus peer mean)

| horizon | n | mean | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-week (k=5, non-overlapping) | 976 | −0.0061% | **−0.216** |
| 1-month (k=21, ~4× overlap) | 976 | −0.0455% | −0.872 |

The devil quintile does **not** measurably underperform its peers at the clean weekly
horizon (*t* = −0.22 — a dead zero). The mildly negative monthly figure is not significant
even before de-overlapping.

## The long/short spread — clean minus devil quintile (folklore: positive)

| cut | n | mean | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-week LS (k=5, non-overlapping) | 976 | +0.0365% | +0.823 | 530/976 = 54.3% [51.2%, 57.4%] |
| 1-month LS (k=21, ~4× overlap) | 976 | +0.1827% | **+2.281** | 532/976 = 54.5% [51.4%, 57.6%] |

The spread carries the folklore's sign (clean beats devil) but the only *t* > 2 is the
**overlap-inflated** monthly cut — see the non-overlapping re-run.

## Random-bucket placebo (20 seeds × 100 draws)

| cut | tail | observed | placebo mean (sd) | p |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-week LS | right | +0.0365% | −0.0000% (0.0396%) | 0.179 |
| 1-month LS | right | +0.1827% | +0.0004% (0.0769%) | **0.006** |

The 1-week spread is indistinguishable from a *random* quintile split (p = 0.18). The
1-month spread sits in the right tail of the random-bucket null (p = 0.006) — but that null
holds the same overlapping cross-sections fixed, so it inherits the same overlap inflation.

## Devil quintile vs the market (SPY) — *artefact, not signal*

| horizon | n | mean | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-week vs SPY | 976 | +0.0729% | +1.954 |
| 1-month vs SPY | 976 | +0.2685% | +3.770 |

The devil quintile *beats* SPY — the **opposite** of the folklore. This is a pure
equal-weight-vs-cap-weight artefact (an equal-weight quintile of mega-caps outran the
cap-weighted index over 2007-2026); it is **not** a devil effect, which is exactly why the
headline test uses the cross-sectionally demeaned (market-neutral) legs above.

## The decisive test — non-overlapping monthly rebalance (spacing = 21)

| cut | n | mean | *t* | placebo p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month LS (clean, non-overlapping) | 232 | +0.2456% | **+1.415** | 0.061 |
| devil quintile demeaned | 232 | −0.0613% | −0.505 | — |

Rebalancing monthly so the windows **do not overlap**, the *t* collapses from +2.28 to
**+1.42** and the placebo softens to p = 0.06 — both short of significance. The apparent
monthly edge was ~4× window overlap, not a real cross-sectional signal.

## Leave-one-year-out jackknife — 1-week LS spread *t*

Full-sample *t* = **+0.823**; across all 20 leave-one-year-out draws the *t* stays in
**[+0.353, +1.960]** — persistently *positive* (the folklore's sign) but never significant,
and not driven by any single year.

## Synthetic positive control (deterministic, no network)

- **Null (bump = 0), 20 seeds:** mean *t* = −0.24 (sd 0.92); |*t*| ≥ 2 in **0/20** seeds —
  the sort detector is well-behaved on the null (many rebalances ⇒ clean small-sample
  behaviour, unlike the template's 18-event calendar).
- **Planted devil drag −1.0% (seed 789):** devil-quintile mean −0.245%, *t* = **−5.58**.
- **Planted devil drag −2.0% (seed 789):** devil-quintile mean −0.427%, *t* = **−8.94** — a
  real planted underperformance is recovered monotonically.

## Verdict

| Axis | Stamp | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Signal — is the effect real?** | **Weak** | The clean, non-overlapping tests are quiet: the 1-week devil quintile is a dead zero (*t* = −0.22) and the 1-week LS spread is noise (*t* = +0.82, placebo p = 0.18). There is a *persistent folklore-signed lean* — LS positive at both horizons, hit rate ~54.5%, jackknife-stable positive — and the monthly spread even hits placebo p = 0.006, but that evaporates the moment you de-overlap the windows (non-overlapping monthly *t* = +1.42, p = 0.06). Borderline, horizon-fragile, and — since a stock's *nominal* mantissa is economically meaningless (split history, not fundamentals) — mechanism-free. |
| **Tradability — survives costs/scale?** | **Mirage** | Nothing to bank. Even the overlap-inflated edge is ~18-25 bps/month gross on a weekly-turnover long/short of ~20 names a side sorted on an arbitrary nominal price digit; net of costs and once de-overlapped it isn't significant. No mechanism, no clean significance, no capacity story. |

**In one sentence:** the "number of the beast" price sort shows a faint, folklore-signed
lean (clean names edge out the 666-touchers) that looks significant only through a
window-overlap illusion and vanishes under a clean non-overlapping test — a Weak,
mechanism-free curiosity and an untradeable Mirage.
